baseline.auditEvidenceLevel: Accepted ADR-0033, canonical Delivery decoding, schema and one-time migration source

inputBoundary.actualInput: current canonical DeliverySnapshot JSON at baedb1ef, including canonical StageRun and SessionBinding fields
inputBoundary.notInput: legacy DSH/StrongFlow snapshot with dshSessionId/codexSessionId; that is only historical precursor evidence and is not passed to the new conversion
inputBoundary.existingMigrationUse: reuse only transaction semantics, source/snapshot/consumed marker shape, digest verification, restart replay, concurrency and rollback tests from 9c4.16.4.8
inputBoundary.identityRule: retain existing canonical ProductSessionId, ExecutionJobId, WorkerSessionId, CodexThreadId, WorkerId, WorkerInstanceId, LeaseId and fencingToken when present; never derive them from temporary directories or dshSessionId

executableWorkRun: exactly one required WorkItem reference resolved from the same Delivery; no null or guessed workItemId
exactly one Attempt owned by the WorkRun; attempt number and source StageRun attempt must be consistent under the accepted contract
exactly one newly issued valid ExecutionLeaseRecord for resume/replacement; historical lease values are provenance and do not grant write authority
at most one accepted Candidate bound to the WorkRun; Candidate identity and revision remain immutable after acceptance
historicalStageRun: StageRun.deliveryTaskId=null is retained as historical provenance only for valid Planner/Human/Delivery-review records
no WorkRun is emitted for a null task mapping, and no WorkItem is inferred from stage, role, actor, or array position
historical evidence/verdict references remain addressable without granting execution authority
workRunInvariants.resume: Controller stops old writes, validates backup and source revision, then issues a new lease/fencing record; it never restores a historical lease or temporary-directory authority

implementation.reader: Delivery::decode_json validates the complete source graph before conversion.
implementation.target: One frozen WorkContract plus WorkItems and non-executable historical WorkRuns; historicalSource preserves the complete source for audit, not runtime writes.
implementation.identity: New contract/item/criterion/run IDs use deterministic namespaced Crockford identifiers; existing execution/session IDs are preserved, never invented. Incomplete or noncanonical execution bindings remain history only.
implementation.candidate: Old Evidence/Verdict is retained as history. It is not promoted to a newly accepted Candidate or completion claim.
implementation.receipt: Source version, source key, exact input digest, output bytes and output digest commit together in one SQLite IMMEDIATE transaction. This is an offline migration receipt, not another runtime state store.
implementation.replay: Identical input returns the same stored bytes after restart. Changed input under the same source identity is rejected. Incomplete or altered receipts are rejected.
implementation.permissions: New private files use 0600; existing parent directory permissions remain unchanged.

cutoverSequence.name: freeze-and-backup
actions: stop new writes and new Worker leases for affected Delivery/Session sources
reach a safe boundary and export a complete consistent source snapshot
verify a restorable backup of that frozen revision
cutoverSequence.gate: The CLI reads only an already frozen offline snapshot; it does not stop a running service.

cutoverSequence.name: convert-once
actions: validate source, preserve the complete read-only history and create canonical new relationships
commit migration receipt and target snapshot atomically
publish backup/output files without overwriting different content
cutoverSequence.gate: Any failed transaction leaves no consumed marker.

cutoverSequence.name: verify-or-restore
actions: restart and compare exact replay bytes
validate generated target objects against canonical schema
verify the backup digest before restoring it to a new path

rollback.offline: The source input is never overwritten. Verify the backup digest and restore to a new path; failed database writes roll back and can be retried.
rollback.production: Production switching and service restart belong to WWC-ER-0006. Before a later production rollback, stop writers and reconcile external effects; restoring a database does not undo Git or provider actions.

checks: cargo test -p winwincode-delivery --test workrun_migration --test sqlite_workrun_migration --test migrate_workrun_cli --locked
implementationBoundary: This E00 slice is a one-time offline migration tool and its contract. WWC-ER-0006 owns production scheduling cutover and deletion of old runtime write paths; the tool neither dispatches jobs nor runs parallel state machines.
